title: DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding
research_question: Can a causal language model gain strong visually rich document understanding by incorporating OCR-derived spatial layout directly into attention, without relying on a heavyweight image encoder?
methodology: DocLLM extends autoregressive language models such as Falcon-1B and Llama2-7B by representing text tokens together with their bounding boxes and introducing disentangled attention over textual and spatial relationships. Pre-training uses autoregressive block infilling over semantically cohesive document text regions instead of relying solely on ordinary next-token prediction. The models are subsequently instruction-tuned on 16 datasets spanning visual question answering, natural-language inference, key-information extraction, and document classification, including both single-page and multi-page documents. Evaluation includes same-dataset/different-split and same-task/different-dataset settings plus ablations of spatial attention, infilling, and decoder masking.

key_findings.finding: DocLLM-7B outperforms the compared state-of-the-art LLM baselines on 14 of the 16 datasets in the same-dataset evaluation setting.
The model generalizes successfully on four of five previously unseen dataset settings, with reported improvements of roughly 15% to 61% for the Llama2-7B-based model on four of those five datasets.

Ablation results show that text-only self-attention has the lowest pre-training next-token-prediction accuracy, while adding spatial interactions improves it; the best reported spatial-attention configuration reaches 39.12 versus 35.43 for text-only attention.

Block infilling with spatial information reaches 39.1 next-token-prediction accuracy in the ablation, compared with 36.2 for causal learning with spatial information and 32.6 for plain causal learning.
A causal decoder performs comparably to, and slightly better than, the tested prefix decoder configurations, so the authors retain the causal architecture.
DocLLM obtains document-layout information from token bounding boxes and deliberately avoids a conventional vision encoder, reducing architectural complexity while retaining spatial structure.

limitations: DocLLM does not directly encode document pixels or visual appearance; the authors identify lightweight visual integration as future work.
The model depends on OCR-derived text and bounding boxes, while the effect of alternative OCR engines and layout parsers is left for future investigation.
The instruction-tuning data is constructed from templated existing datasets rather than crowdsourced natural instructions and preferences.
The ablation experiments are resource-constrained to a sampled subset of 100,000 pre-training chunks and evaluation on 1,000 unseen documents.
The paper's official public repository contains the paper description and results but does not expose the full training implementation required to reproduce the reported models.
Not all data used to create the complete instruction-tuning mixture is released as a single reproducible dataset.
raw_claims: DocLLM models document text together with token bounding boxes.
It extends causal language-model attention with disentangled spatial attention.
The architecture does not require a conventional image encoder.
Pre-training uses an autoregressive block-infilling objective over document text.
Instruction tuning spans VQA, NLI, key-information extraction, and document classification.
The reported instruction-tuning data contains 635,883 training instances and 96,919 testing instances.
DocLLM-7B is based on Llama2-7B and DocLLM-1B is based on Falcon-1B.
DocLLM is evaluated on both familiar dataset splits and held-out datasets with the same task types.
DocLLM-7B outperforms the compared LLM baselines on 14 of 16 datasets in the main same-dataset setting.
Spatial information improves the pre-training ablation over text-only attention.
Block infilling with spatial information achieves the best reported objective-level ablation result.
The authors leave comparisons across OCR engines and layout parsers to future work.
The authors propose adding visual information to DocLLM in a lightweight manner in future work.
